react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics dataset discriminates control from treatment groups through a profoundly disrupted tryptophan metabolism axis. Across three complementary analytical paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 1.46×10⁻¹⁵), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p=1.79×10⁻⁷), and Mummichog m/z-direct network activity (p=0.00319) — KEGG:hsa00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' emerges as the unambiguous cross-paradigm winner, ranking first in all three tools. L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the entry-point substrate whose differential abundance anchors the entire signal. Downstream, serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598) — canonically synthesised from tryptophan via the aromatic amine branch — are both differentially abundant, defining REACT:R-HSA-209931 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' as a second significant Reactome hit (FDR 2.81×10⁻⁸, rank 5 in RaMP). Indoleacetaldehyde (C00637) and tryptamine (C00398) extend the signal through the indole/pyrrole sub-branch. The kynurenine arm of the pathway is represented by quinolinic acid (C03722), the penultimate NAD⁺ precursor, confirming that the treatment perturbation spans both the neurotransmitter-synthesis and the energy/cofactor arms of tryptophan catabolism. The absence of tryptophan intermediates in the pyrophosphate, glucose and succinic acid clusters — which appear only in low-ranked Mummichog secondary hits — indicates these metabolites likely reflect downstream metabolic cross-talk rather than primary pathway drivers. The convergent tryptophan-metabolism signal across ORA and network paradigms with eight matched input features positions L-tryptophan catabolism as the biological narrative most consistent with the multi-paradigm evidence.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converged on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA ranked KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" first (FDR below 1e-15), with six input metabolites mapping to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, indoleacetaldehyde (indol-3-ylacetaldehyde), tryptamine, and quinolinic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) first with p = 1.79×10⁻⁷, hitting the same five tryptophan-derived compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct network activity analysis confirmed this pathway at rank 1 (p = 0.002) against the empirical human_mfn network, extending the hit to eight matched features. WikiPathways WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism) also ranked among RaMP's top hits alongside WP:WP3925 (Amino acid metabolism), with succinic acid appearing as an additional member of the amino-acid cluster. The convergent signal spans the neurotransmitter arm (serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde) and the NAD⁺-precursor arm (quinolinic acid) of tryptophan catabolism. The driver metabolites — L-tryptophan as entry-point substrate, serotonin as the central neurotransmitter intermediate, and quinolinic acid as a downstream kynurenine-pathway product — are all verified members of the top-ranked KEGG pathway.

RaMP multi-database ORA ranked KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' first (FDR = 1.46e-15, fold enrichment = 857.8), with six input metabolites mapping to this pathway: quinolinic acid, melatonin, indoleacetaldehyde, serotonin, L-tryptophan, and tryptamine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked hsa00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' first (p = 1.79e-07), hitting five tryptophan-derived metabolites: L-tryptophan, melatonin, serotonin, indoleacetaldehyde, and tryptamine. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis ranked 'Tryptophan metabolism' on the human_mfn network first (p = 0.0014), with eight matched features including L-tryptophan, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, serotonin, melatonin, and quinolinic acid.
